newsitem.title: USA: LatAm debt mixed in narrow, pre-holiday ranges.
newsitem.headline: LatAm debt mixed in narrow, pre-holiday ranges.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices clung to narrow ranges Wednesday, traders said.
Many fund managers and Brady bond traders were taking vacation ahead of the U.S. Labor Day long weekend.
"There has been very little client flow back and forth," said a Brady trader at a U.S. money center bank. "It's dead."
Dealers said that Argentine paper, which surged Tuesday on optimism that Congress would approve the government's fiscal austerity package, slipped Wednesday with U.S. Treasuries.
Argentine FRBs slipped 3/8 for a bid price of 77-5/8, after a morning burst of buying out of Buenos Aires found little support.
Walter Molano, director of Latin American economic research at Swiss Bank, said some international investors seemed to be taking profits, despite the optimism of local players in Argentina.
"The local markets seems to be most optimistic," Molano said. "There thee is a lot of optimism about passage of reform package by the Congress."
The budget and finance committee of Argentina's lower house of Congress approved the measuries Wednesday and passed them on for debate int he Chamber of Deputies.

Marcelo Fleury, vice president at Garband Corporates, said that the Brady market was holding onto its strong gains since last Friday, and that Brazilian paper fared well despite a dearth of fresh news.
"Today's ranges have been very tight," Fleury said. "In September this market is goign to come back with significant volume."
Brazilian Cs picked up 3/8 to 65-1/8, while IDUs slipped 1/8 to 95-3/4.

Across the Latin debt markets, investors kept prices well bid amid an ongoing vigil to determine whether any of the nations would follow Mexico's strategy of swapping its collateralized Brady debt for fresh global bonds.
"People are keeping on top of any or all annoucnements about buybacks of plans in Argentina, Mexico, Brazil or Venezuela," one trader said. "That certainly has helped give a bid side to the prices."
